breast cancer cells with stem cell properties are more likely to cause cancer, are more likely to spread to other parts of the body, are more resistant to chemotherapy and radiation therapy and are more difficult to kill with drugs.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification, characterization and therapeutic targeting of BCSCs in breast cancer.
understanding the biology of breast cancer stem cell and their role in breast cancer initiation, progression, metastases and therapy resistance.
the identification of the molecular pathways that are critical to the survival and function of BCSCs in the different molecular subgroups of breast cancer.

we have a long way to go, but the future is very promising.

The main takeaway from our work is that
BCSCs are not a single entity and that the heterogeneity of BCSCs is likely a reflection of the heterogeneity of breast cancer.
BCSCs are not a homogenous population and that the heterogeneity in this population may be due to differences in the molecular signature and/or the microenvironment in which the cells exist.
